# Load and Inspect Data
Apparently you don't have to convert categorical into numerical 
values in R, it just automatically labels them with the as.factor function

```{r}
sum(is.na(data$ai_tools_used))
head(data)
print("GLIMPSE")
glimpse(data)
print("SUMMARY")
summary(data)
```

# Preprocessing Data
```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    n_languages  = str_count(languages_used,  ";") + 1,
    n_frameworks = str_count(frameworks_used, ";") + 1,
    n_databases  = str_count(databases_used,  ";") + 1,
    n_cloud      = str_count(cloud_platforms_used, ";") + 1
  )

# --- Binary flags for top 10 languages ---
top_languages <- data %>%
  pull(languages_used) %>%
  str_split(";") %>%
  unlist() %>%
  str_trim() %>%
  table() %>%
  sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  names()

for (lang in top_languages) {
  col_name <- paste0("lang_", make_clean_names(lang))
  data[[col_name]] <- as.integer(str_detect(data$languages_used, fixed(lang)))
}

lang_cols <- paste0("lang_", make_clean_names(top_languages))
```

```{r}
# --- Encode categoricals as numeric (required by KNN) ---
data_model <- data %>%
  filter(annual_salary_usd > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    # Target — factor with 5 levels
    job_satisfaction = factor(job_satisfaction),

    # Ordinal encodings (numeric ranking)
    education_num = case_when(
      education_level == "Less than high school" ~ 1,
      education_level == "Some high school"      ~ 2,
      education_level == "High school diploma"   ~ 3,
      education_level == "Some college"          ~ 4,
      education_level == "Associate's degree"    ~ 5,
      education_level == "Bachelor's degree"     ~ 6,
      education_level == "Master's degree"       ~ 7,
      education_level == "Professional degree"   ~ 8,
      education_level == "Doctoral degree"       ~ 9
    ),
    company_size_num = case_when(
      company_size == "1-10"       ~ 1,
      company_size == "11-50"      ~ 2,
      company_size == "51-200"     ~ 3,
      company_size == "201-1000"   ~ 4,
      company_size == "1001-5000"  ~ 5,
      company_size == "5000-10000" ~ 6,
      company_size == "10000+"     ~ 7
    ),
    burnout_num = case_when(
      burnout_frequency == "Never"     ~ 1,
      burnout_frequency == "Rarely"    ~ 2,
      burnout_frequency == "Sometimes" ~ 3,
      burnout_frequency == "Often"     ~ 4,
      burnout_frequency == "Always"    ~ 5
    ),
    ai_usage_num = case_when(
      ai_usage_frequency == "Never"               ~ 1,
      ai_usage_frequency == "Rarely"              ~ 2,
      ai_usage_frequency == "Monthly"             ~ 3,
      ai_usage_frequency == "Weekly"              ~ 4,
      ai_usage_frequency == "Daily"               ~ 5,
      ai_usage_frequency == "Multiple times daily"~ 6
    ),
    remote_pref_num = case_when(
      remote_work_preference_1to5 == 1 ~ 1,
      remote_work_preference_1to5 == 2 ~ 2,
      remote_work_preference_1to5 == 3 ~ 3,
      remote_work_preference_1to5 == 4 ~ 4,
      remote_work_preference_1to5 == 5 ~ 5
    ),

    # Nominal → integer encoding
    gender_num            = as.integer(factor(gender)),
    role_num              = as.integer(factor(role)),
    country_num           = as.integer(factor(country)),
    employment_num        = as.integer(factor(employment_status)),
    work_mode_num         = as.integer(factor(work_mode)),
    primary_os_num        = as.integer(factor(primary_os)),
    ai_sentiment_num      = as.integer(factor(ai_sentiment)),
    ai_threat_num         = as.integer(factor(ai_job_threat_perception)),
    learning_source_num   = as.integer(factor(primary_learning_source)),
    looking_for_job_num   = as.integer(factor(looking_for_job))
  ) %>%
  select(
    job_satisfaction,
    # Numeric as-is
    age, years_of_experience, coding_hours_per_week,
    annual_salary_usd, career_satisfaction,
    ai_productivity_boost_pct, open_source_contributor,
    n_languages, n_frameworks, n_databases, n_cloud,
    # Ordinal encodings
    education_num, company_size_num, burnout_num,
    ai_usage_num, remote_pref_num,
    # Nominal encodings
    gender_num, role_num, country_num, employment_num,
    work_mode_num, primary_os_num, ai_sentiment_num,
    ai_threat_num, learning_source_num, looking_for_job_num,
    # Language flags
    all_of(lang_cols)
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

cat("Rows ready for KNN:", nrow(data_model), "\n")

```
